name: The crossroads: MLK Jr. Dr. and Fairburn Rd.
note: Old Gordon Road meets Fairburn Road. Planned as a town center in 1955, 1970, 1977 and 2020.

name: Community Food Center, 3500 MLK Jr. Dr.
note: Atlanta Community Food Bank's free, client-choice grocery in a former Family Dollar, opened August 2025.

name: Fire Station 9 and the commercial strip
note: Dollar General, City Takers church and Fire Station 9 share the blocks around the food center.

name: Former Margaret Fain School
note: Built 1927. Called 'the most important building in the community' in 1955. Douglass High ninth-grade campus from 2022; slated to close.

name: Old Adamsville Recreation Center
note: Senior programs midweek; serves as a warming center.

name: C. T. Martin Natatorium and Recreation Center
note: 3201 MLK Jr. Dr. 50-meter pool and therapy pool; renamed for Councilmember C. T. Martin in 2017.

name: Cascade Family Skating
note: Regional landmark for young people; featured in the 2006 film ATL.

name: Adamsville Regional Health Center
note: Fulton County health center. The 1955 report praised 'a fine county health center.'

name: Wilson Mill Park
note: Where most community events happen, residents say. The 1970 plan proposed expanding it.

name: Jackson Memorial Baptist Church
note: Its pastor appears on the 2023 Adamsville Legacy mural.

name: L. P. Miles Elementary
note: Began in 1907 as Bethlehem Church School, the first school for African American children in Adamsville-Boulder Park.

name: Benjamin E. Mays High School
note: Residents remember it as one of the most desirable high schools in the city.
